title: NumPy: ndarray, dtype and how it sits in memory

videos.script: A Python list of numbers is a list of objects. Each one lives somewhere else in memory. {{list}} A NumPy array is different. It is one block of bytes, and every number in it has the same type. {{block}} That is why it is four times smaller. It is why arithmetic on it needs no loop. {{why}} And it is why it is strict. Add five to a small integer at the edge of its range, and it wraps round to a negative number. No error. {{wrap}} This lesson reads the shape and the type of an array before trusting it. {{shape}} It looks at how a table sits in memory, as a flat row of bytes with a rule for reading it. {{strides}} And it finds the change that shows up somewhere else: a slice that is not a copy. {{view}} Last, what NumPy 2 changed, for all the code written before it. {{end}}
